title: One question per card
hook: A card asking three things can hide which one you missed.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: Split a compound prompt into separately checkable cues.

objective: Split a compound prompt into separately checkable cues.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: A card asking three things can hide which one you missed. Which card makes a missed item identifiable? Correct option: One target per cue. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Separate cues expose separate gaps. A correct answer to one cue does not establish knowledge of the other two.
claims.source: Roediger & Karpicke (2006), Test-Enhanced Learning, Psychological Science 17(3),249–255, DOI10.1111/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x; publisher abstract retrieved 2026-10-13: https://www.psychologicalscience.org/journals/psychological-science/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x/ . Fixture mappings and rules are explicit conventions, not empirical demonstrations. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

recall.question: A card asks 'Who signed the treaty, where and when?' and you get it half right. What change shows which part you missed?
options: Add more detail to the same card
Answer the same card faster next time
Split it into three cards, one fact each
recall.why: With one target per cue, each miss points at one fact; a compound card hides which part failed.
